raw_text:
Summary & constraints
- Client: 36-year-old male recreational lifter, 6 months post right medial meniscus tear. Surgeon cleared for low-impact strength work but NO jumping and NO deep knee flexion under load (avoid loaded squats below ~60–70° knee flexion). Full gym access. Goal: strength and return to skiing next season.
- Key considerations: protect the right knee by avoiding deep loaded knee flexion, high-impact/plyometric loading, twisting under load, and start with controlled range of motion and progressive eccentric control. Prioritise hip and posterior chain strength, single-leg strength in safe ranges, trunk control, neuromuscular balance, and gradual return to dynamic/perturbation work that is low-impact.

Programme structure (12 weeks)
- 3 phases: Foundational (Weeks 1–4), Strength Build (Weeks 5–8), Ski-Prep Transition (Weeks 9–12).
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (2 lower-body–focused, 2 upper-body/ full-body accessory). This gives enough volume for strength while leaving recovery and low-impact conditioning days.
- Progression: increase load weekly by small increments (2.5–5% when reps remain in target) or add reps/sets, then a short deload in Week 7 and Week 11 as noted. RPE target: 7–9 for main lifts when pushing; avoid max testing until Week 12 if desired.
- Warm-up: each session 8–12 minutes: general cardio 5 min (bike/row/elliptical low-impact), mobility and dynamic warm-up focusing on hips, ankles, thoracic spine, glutes, and knee-friendly activation (e.g., glute bridges, banded monster walks, single-leg balance). Finish with 2–3 ramp sets for main lifts.
- Cool-down & recovery: 5–10 min mobility, soft tissue work as needed. Recommend sleep 7–9 hrs/night, protein ~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, caloric intake set to slight surplus if aiming to gain strength/muscle (≈+200–350 kcal/day) or maintenance if not. Hydration and anti-inflammatory management per physician if needed.

Exercise selection rules for knee safety
- Avoid barbell back/front squats beyond ~60–70° knee flexion. Substitute or limit range with box squats to a safe height, goblet or front-loaded partial squats to a controlled depth, belt squats, and hack squats with limited ROM if comfortable.
- Emphasize hip-dominant lifts: Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts, split-stance RDLs.
- Single-leg options: reverse lunges to short step, Bulgarian split squats with limited knee bend (elevate front foot to reduce depth if necessary), step-ups to controlled height, single-leg Romanian deadlifts, and constrained-range single-leg press.
- Avoid jumping, depth drops, and high-impact plyometrics. Include low-impact dynamic drills later in programme (low-height box step-downs, controlled lateral weight shifts, low-intensity ski-specific dynamic balance).

Phase 1 — Foundational (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: rebuild control, correct strength imbalances, increase posterior chain capacity, early hypertrophy to support later strength. Load: moderate (RPE 6–8).

Weekly layout (4 days)
- Day A: Lower — Hip-dominant + limited-knee quadriceps
- Day B: Upper — Horizontal/vertical push/pull + core
- Day C: Lower — Single-leg emphasis + trunk/stability
- Day D: Upper/Full — Overhead, posterior chain assistance, conditioning

Week 1–4 details (progress weekly by adding 2–5% load or 1 rep per set):
Day A — Lower (Strength/Hypertrophy)
1. Romanian Deadlift (RDL) — 4 sets x 6–8 reps (2–3 min rest). Focus hip hinge, slow eccentric.
2. Box Squat to a high box (limit knee flexion) — 4 x 6 (use a height that gives ~60–70° or less knee flexion). Pause 1s at bottom.
3. Bulgarian Split Squat — 3 x 8 each leg (reduce depth on injured side as needed; can do rear-foot-elevated to shallower depth).
4. Glute Bridge / Barbell Hip Thrust — 3 x 8–10.
5. Banded Lateral Walks — 3 x 30–40 steps (activation).
6. Farmer Carry (heavy) — 3 x 30–45 sec.

Day B — Upper
1. Barbell Bench Press (or dumbbell) — 4 x 5–6.
2. Bent-Over Row — 4 x 6–8.
3. Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press — 3 x 8–10.
4. Pull-up (assisted if needed) or Lat Pulldown — 3 x 6–8.
5. Face Pulls — 3 x 12–15.
6. Pallof Press — 3 x 12 each side.

Day C — Lower (Single-leg + stability)
1. Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — 4 x 6–8 each leg (light to moderate).
2. Step-ups onto 20–25 cm box — 4 x 6–8 each leg (control; no jumping).
3. Cable or machine leg press — 3 x 8–10 (limit ROM to safe depth).
4. Nordic hamstring curls (assisted) or eccentric hamstring work — 3 x 6–8.
5. Single-leg balance/perturbation drills (wobble pad, eyes closed) — 3 x 30–45 sec.
6. Ab wheel rollouts or Pallof progression — 3 x 8–12.

Day D — Upper/Full
1. Deadlift variation (trap bar deadlift, lighter than RDL day) — 3 x 5.
2. Incline Dumbbell Press — 3 x 8.
3. One-arm DB Row — 3 x 8 each side.
4. Reverse Hyper or Back Extension (limited flexion) — 3 x 10.
5. Lateral Raises — 3 x 12–15.
6. Conditioning: Low-impact steady-state cardio 20–25 min (bike/elliptical) or interval 6 x 1 min hard/2 min easy on bike if tolerated.

Notes Weeks 1–4:
- Emphasize tempo control (2–3s eccentric). Watch knee during split squats/step-ups and reduce depth if pain/increased swelling.
- Encourage adherence to protein and total calories; aim for protein ~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day.

Phase 2 — Strength Build (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: increase absolute strength, keep knee-safe ranges, raise intensity. Load: higher (RPE 7.5–9). Slight deload Week 7 (reduce volume ~30% but keep intensity).

Weekly layout unchanged. Main changes: heavier loads, lower reps for key lifts, increased accessory intensity.

Weeks 5–8 details:
Day A — Lower (Strength focus)
1. Trap-Bar Deadlift — 5 sets x 3–5 reps (2–3 min rest).
2. Box Front Squat (or belt squat) — 5 x 4–6 (box set to limit depth).
3. Romanian Deadlift (heavy) or Deficit RDL — 3 x 5–6.
4. Barbell Hip Thrust — 4 x 5–6 (heavier).
5. Heavy Farmer Carry or Suitcase Carry — 4 x 30–45 sec.

Day B — Upper (Strength)
1. Barbell Bench Press — 5 x 3–5.
2. Weighted Pull-up or Heavy Lat Pulldown — 4 x 4–6.
3. Seated Military Press — 4 x 5–6.
4. Chest-supported Row — 3 x 6–8.
5. Core: Hanging Leg Raise — 3 x 8–12.

Day C — Lower (Single-leg strength & knee control)
1. Bulgarian Split Squat (weighted, reduced depth if needed) — 4 x 6 each.
2. Single-leg RDL (heavy) — 4 x 5–6 each.
3. Step-downs (controlled) from low box — 3 x 8 each (eccentric control emphasis).
4. Leg Press (short ROM, heavy) — 4 x 6–8.
5. Nordic curl or glute-ham raise — 3 x 6–8.
6. Hip abductor machine or banded work — 3 x 12–15.

Day D — Upper/Full & Conditioning
1. Deadlift variation light or paused (technique) — 3 x 3–5.
2. Incline Bench Press — 4 x 6.
3. T-bar or landmine rows — 4 x 6–8.
4. Rear-delt/face pull superset — 3 x 12–15.
5. Low-impact interval conditioning: 8–10 rounds 30s high/90s easy on bike or skierg.

Week 7: reduce volume (~30% fewer sets) but keep 1–2 heavy sets on main lifts to maintain neural stimulus.

Phase 3 — Ski-Prep Transition (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: convert strength into ski-specific durability, lateral strength, dynamic stability and gradual re-introduction of low-impact dynamic drills. Continue avoiding high-impact jumping; introduce controlled lateral hops only if surgeon approves and no symptoms (but default: step-overs, low-box lateral step-downs). Week 11 is a deload. Week 12 is an assessment week (test 3–5 rep maxes carefully or perform functional ski simulation drills).

Weekly layout: 4 days, but sessions include more multi-planar work and balance.

Weeks 9–12 details:
Day A — Lower (Strength & lateral bias)
1. Trap-bar deadlift or sumo deadlift — 4 x 3–5.
2. Lateral step-ups onto 20–25 cm box — 4 x 6 each side (controlled).
3. Belt squat or hack squat limited ROM — 4 x 6–8.
4. Reverse lunge to balance — 3 x 8 each.
5. Side-band resisted ski-simulation (band across hips) — 3 x 30–45 sec.
6. Loaded carry: suitcase or offset carry — 3 x 30–45 sec.

Day B — Upper / Power (No jumps)
1. Push press (light-moderate) — 4 x 3–5 (explosive but no impact).
2. Weighted chin-ups — 4 x 4–6.
3. Incline DB bench — 3 x 6–8.
4. Single-arm landmine row — 3 x 8 each.
5. Core: anti-rotation holds and chops — 3 x 8–10 each.

Day C — Lower (Single-leg, eccentric control, ski-specific)
1. Single-leg box squats to controlled height (~60° range) — 4 x 5–6 each.
2. Single-leg RDL with knee drive (return to balance) — 4 x 6 each.
3. Controlled lateral lowering (lateral step-down) — 3 x 8–10.
4. Nordic hamstring curls or weighted GHR — 3 x 6–8.
5. Balance/proprioception circuit: single-leg holds with perturbations, eyes closed — 4 rounds.

Day D — Full / Conditioning / Mobility
1. Deadlift or Romanian variant — 3 x 4–6.
2. Overhead press or push press — 3 x 5–6.
3. Rows/cable pulls — 3 x 8.
4. Low-impact ski-specific conditioning: Skierg intervals 8–12 x 30s on/60s off or bike single-leg intervals to simulate unilateral load (if tolerated).
5. Mobility: hip external rotation, ankle dorsiflexion, thoracic rotations.

Week 11: deload (reduce volume ~30–40%, maintain intensity for 1–2 sets).

Week 12: assessment & sport prep
- Session content: submaximal 3–5 RM testing for trap-bar deadlift and a safe squat variant, single-leg strength assessment (single-leg RDL x 5RM), and functional screens (single-leg balance, step-down control). Avoid true 1RM heavy testing on knee if any discomfort.
- If cleared and asymptomatic, introduce very low box lateral hops or quick step transitions (low amplitude, focus on control) to reintroduce dynamic movement.

Progression examples & loading guidance
- For strength lifts (e.g., deadlift, bench): weekly increase 2.5–5% when you can complete top set target reps with good form.
- For hypertrophy/accessory: increase reps/sets before raising load. Use RPE 7–8 for moderate sets; last set near RPE 8–9 when loading heavy.
- If pain, swelling, or decreased function occurs, reduce depth/volume and consult the surgeon/physio.

Knee-monitoring & rehab integration
- Have client maintain a joint-status log: pain (0–10), swelling, stiffness each day and after heavy sessions. Any increase in effusion or persistent pain gets a 72-hour modification (reduce knee loading, consult physio).
- Keep a physio or mobility routine: daily light banded knee/quad cross-friction if advised, foam rolling of quads/hamstrings/IT band, and 10 min of hip/glute activation pre/post session.
- Continue working with the surgeon/physio for any return-to-impact milestones.

Nutrition & recovery (brief)
- Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day. Example: for a 80 kg client = 128–160 g protein/day.
- Calories: maintenance +200–300 kcal for strength gain; maintain if body composition is adequate.
- Timing: protein distribution across meals (20–40 g every 3–4 hrs). Post-workout carbohydrate + protein can aid recovery.
- Supplementation (optional): creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day for strength gains; vitamin D if low; omega-3 for general inflammation support (consult physician).
- Recovery: sleep 7–9 hrs, prioritize rest days, use ice only if acute swelling post-session; contrast or active recovery on off days (walking, swim).

Return-to-ski timeline & drills (late phase)
- Weeks 9–12: introduce ski-specific unilateral endurance and low-impact dynamic work (skierg, edge-holding isometrics, lateral step-downs).
- Off-snow pre-season: low-impact slide board (short duration) if knee tolerates, and low-amplitude lateral hops only if cleared.
- On-snow: start with groomed runs, moderate pace, avoid off-piste/dynamic jumping initially. Progress to full activity over a few weeks if no symptoms.

Sample week (Week 6 example)
- Mon (Day A): Trap-bar Deadlift 5x3; Box Front Squat 5x5; RDL 3x5; Hip Thrust 4x6; Farmer Carry 4x30s.
- Tue (Day B): Bench 5x3; Weighted Pull-ups 4x4; Seated Press 4x6; Chest-supported Row 3x6; Hanging Leg Raise 3x10.
- Wed: off / active recovery (mobility, light bike 20 min).
- Thu (Day C): Bulgarian Split 4x6 each; Single-leg RDL 4x5 each; Step-down 3x8 each; Leg Press 4x6; Nordic 3x6.
- Fri (Day D): Light Deadlift/Technique 3x3; Incline DB Press 4x6; T-bar Row 4x6; Face pulls 3x15; Bike intervals 8x30s/90s.
- Sat/Sun: 1 day active recovery, 1 rest.

Safety & final notes
- Keep regular contact with client’s surgeon/physio if symptoms change.
- Avoid testing 1RM squats or heavy deep squat movement until knee is fully asymptomatic and surgeon clears.
- Emphasize quality of movement, single-leg control, and posterior chain strength — these will transfer best to skiing performance while keeping the knee safe.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into printable week-by-week templates with exact percentages for main lifts if you give current 3–5RM numbers.
- Provide progression tables, warm-up routines, or specific rehab exercises your physio recommends to integrate.
